content:
This is a thread for questions about mathlib's security policy (which will apply to mathlib4, mathlib-ci, and a few other repos.

The text of the policy can be found here.

The maintainers are not experts on security, ...

Why give the game away? Why not "The maintainers are devoted to keeping all of..."?
I saw the same phrasing elsewhere and figured we should also be honest!

Kevin Buzzard said:

The maintainers are not experts on security, ...

Why give the game away? Why not "The maintainers are devoted to keeping all of..."?

This is why maybe? https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_through_obscurity

I don't buy it. There is not some rule which says we have to announce all facts. Just don't say it -- it doesn't need saying. It's nothing to do with security through obscurity, it's to do with not explicitly inviting hacks.

Kevin Buzzard said:

I don't buy it. There is not some rule which says we have to announce all facts. Just don't say it -- it doesn't need saying. It's nothing to do with security through obscurity, it's to do with not explicitly inviting hacks.

That's not a realistic scenario (and identifying your threat model is cybersec 101*). The kind of people who would assume such an invitation will not require more than a few seconds to find out who's who and what their expertise is and isn't. By being transparent, you are setting expectations for benign users. Separately, maybe mathlib should perform audits of its CI from time to time. Most cyber attacks happen on scale with a lot of automation anyway (imagine 10000 repos getting attacked using the same vulnerability to hide a trojan in as many machines as possible).

*Reference: https://textbook.cs161.org/textbook_full.pdf
